1	# HARD CONTRACT (read this before doing anything)
2	
3	> **Shared.** Read FIRST — before any phase and before any other file — by both `/review` and `/deep-review`, from the head of the command spine.
4	
5	This command is an **orchestrator** — its sole job is to execute the phases its command spine lists, in order. The phases are NOT optional, NOT a menu, and NOT a template for inspiration. If you find yourself "skipping ahead to the report" or "improvising a summary file," STOP — that is a failure mode. Follow the prose step-by-step, in numerical phase order, top to bottom.
6	
7	**Output paths — non-negotiable:**
8	
9	- **WRITE only to `.turingmind/`** in the user's project. Specifically: `.turingmind/state/<$PHASE_ID>.json` where `<$PHASE_ID>` is the full resolved phase directory name (Phase 4.5; see Phase 0.5 for the exact filename rule — never abbreviate), optional `.turingmind/reviews/<ISO timestamp>/` (Phase 4.5 snapshot), `.turingmind/REVIEW.md` (only via Finalize mode), and the transient scratch paths `.turingmind/git-guard/` (the before/after git snapshot and the block log), `.turingmind/fixstage/` and `.turingmind/fixcheck/` (fix-agent scratch, removed after each finding).
10	- **NEVER write to `.planning/`** — that namespace belongs to GSD. The tool READS PLAN.md/SPEC.md/RESEARCH.md from there (Phase 1.5) but writes nothing.
11	- **NEVER write per-phase review files** like `.planning/phases/<id>/<NN>-REVIEW.md` or `<NN>-DEEP-REVIEW.md` even if you see GSD/other plugins creating files in that location. **This tool does not produce per-phase artifacts in `.planning/`.** The single authoritative artifact is `.turingmind/REVIEW.md`, written by `--finalize`.
12	- Mid-loop `/review` and `/deep-review` invocations **print findings to the chat transcript only**. No file write of the report itself. State file under `.turingmind/state/` is the only review state persisted by a non-finalize pass (the scratch paths above are transient).
13	
14	**Phase progression — non-negotiable:**
15	
16	- Announce each phase as you enter it with one line: `✓ Phase N — <name>` (or `⊘ Phase N — <name> (skipped: <reason>)` if a skip condition fires). The user reads these announcements to verify the orchestrator is on track.
17	- Load every phase file with the **Read tool** — never with `cat`, `head`, `sed` or any other Bash command — and Read it BEFORE you announce that phase. The Read of a phase's file is the record that its instructions were loaded; an announcement line is for the human reader and is never evidence that a phase ran. Write announcements in your reply text, never inside a Bash command.
18	- Phase 4 (Render) MUST be followed by Phase 4.5 (Persist state). Phase 4.5 MUST be followed by Phase 5 (Interactive fix loop) UNLESS one of Phase 5's documented skip conditions applies.
19	- The presence of Phase 5 as the next step is non-negotiable for any stateful invocation with findings. "I already rendered the report so I'm done" is the failure mode — Phase 5 is part of the user-facing contract, not a polish step.
20	- **Subagents run in the foreground.** Every `Task` (Agent) call this command makes sets `run_in_background: false` — triage, the Phase-2 reviewers and the `fix` agent alike. Each phase collects its agents' results in the very next turn; a background dispatch ends the turn before they return and the review stops mid-pass with nothing collected. Parallel calls in one tool-use block still run concurrently.
21	
22	**If unsure, surface the uncertainty rather than improvise.** Print "I'm uncertain about <specific phase or step> — orchestrator prose is ambiguous here" and stop. That is always preferable to inventing behavior that violates the contract above.
23

4	> run its seat line.** This file binds the helper paths every later phase uses. Nothing else reads it;
5	> nothing else may re-resolve them.

Every containment decision now calls the ONE tested `scripts/guard.py` (fail-closed: empty root/path, non-dir root, and any escape all refuse; missing-path TOLERANT: a deleted-but-in-diff file is judged lexically; relative `--path` values resolve against `--root`). Bind it here with the SAME TRUST-01 resolver that binds `$SCORE_PY`/`$CONFIG_PY` (guard.py sits in the same `scripts/` dir):
8	
9	`$VC_ROOT`, `$GUARD_PY`, `$CONFIG_PY`, `$SCORE_PY` are bound HERE, once, and carried forward like `$CONFIG_*` — later phases substitute the resolved absolute paths and never re-resolve. The spine's seat line is the only place the load-time token is spelled on this path; the resolver body reads the value the seat exported. The owner's dev override is the env var `VIBE_CHECK_PLUGIN_ROOT` (exported by the owner; the recommended dev workflow is `claude --plugin-dir <repo>/plugins/vibe-check`, which makes arm (1) the working tree).
10	
11	Run the block below in the SAME Bash call as the spine's seat line, seat first. If the two end up in
12	separate Bash calls, re-emit the seat line at the top of the call that runs this block — each Bash call
13	may be a fresh shell, and an unset seat value makes every consumer take its terminal arm.
14	
15	```bash
16	# TRUST-01 resolver — the trusted plugin root arrives from the SEAT line above (a loader substitution the
17	# reviewed repo cannot reach). Arm (2) is an env var the OWNER exports (`VIBE_CHECK_PLUGIN_ROOT`) — never
18	# read from the reviewed repo. There is NO repo-relative arm and NO cache-glob/marketplace arm. If BOTH arms
19	# are empty every consumer takes its terminal arm.
20	VC_ROOT="${VIBE_CHECK_PLUGIN_ROOT_SUBST:-}"
21	[ -z "$VC_ROOT" ] && VC_ROOT="${VIBE_CHECK_PLUGIN_ROOT:-}"
22	# (3) terminal arm is PER CONSUMER (D-13): guard/score FAIL CLOSED on empty; config DEGRADES to defaults.
23	GUARD_PY="";  [ -n "$VC_ROOT" ] && [ -f "$VC_ROOT/scripts/guard.py" ]  && GUARD_PY="$VC_ROOT/scripts/guard.py"
24	CONFIG_PY=""; [ -n "$VC_ROOT" ] && [ -f "$VC_ROOT/scripts/config.py" ] && CONFIG_PY="$VC_ROOT/scripts/config.py"
25	SCORE_PY="";  [ -n "$VC_ROOT" ] && [ -f "$VC_ROOT/scripts/score.py" ]  && SCORE_PY="$VC_ROOT/scripts/score.py"
26	# /TRUST-01 resolver
27	# Terminal arm: $GUARD_PY EMPTY. Every consumer FAILS CLOSED on that (treats the
28	# path as NOT contained / refuses) — a security guard degrades to refusal, never
29	# to pass-through. (Contrast: $CONFIG_PY degrades to defaults; $SCORE_PY halts.)
30	# Print what was bound, so every later phase can substitute the RESOLVED absolute paths.
31	printf 'VC_ROOT=%s\nGUARD_PY=%s\nCONFIG_PY=%s\nSCORE_PY=%s\n' "$VC_ROOT" "$GUARD_PY" "$CONFIG_PY" "$SCORE_PY"
32	```

35	
36	Carry these forward for the whole invocation: `$VC_ROOT`, `$GUARD_PY`, `$CONFIG_PY`, `$SCORE_PY`.
37	Later phases substitute the RESOLVED ABSOLUTE PATHS into their own Bash calls and never re-resolve.
38	
39	**Why arm (1) is an env var and not the load-time token.** The bytes of this file arrive through
40	`Read` and are NOT loader-processed — the token would survive here as dead literal text. The spine
41	that read this file IS loader-processed, so the spine performs the substitution once, on its seat

5

The by-hand "apply the formula / carry-forward / dedup / threshold / silenced / in_diff override" prose has been REMOVED (D-09) — there is no longer a manual path that can produce a scored finding. **A finding has a `band`/`orchestrator_score` ONLY because the script wrote one; a finding that never went through the script has no band to render (the un-skippability that is CORE-03's point).** This wiring does NOT change scoring behavior — the script reproduces `templates/scoring.md` exactly (behavior-preserving extraction, pinned by `scripts/test_score.py`).
7	
8	The orchestrator still does the work the script CANNOT (it is a pure function — no git/file/shell I/O): it collects raw facts (the per-finding `source_window`, `canonical_line_content` from the HEAD read, the `changed_line_ranges`, the `$REVIEWED_UNION` set), and it parses + dispatches.

18	esac
